historical_sanity_anchor.baseline: Historical 11th Army fought through Liuyang/Ningxiang and isolated Changsha before taking the city on 18 June. Branch Phase A began 29 days earlier, Japanese logistics/engineer process is better, and Chinese command is more explicitly preserving field armies; therefore the operational sequence is retained but local battles are adjudicated from branch state rather than date-shift copying.

daily_phase_outline.result: Japanese eastern and western wings tighten pressure on Liuyang and Ningxiang approach systems. Chinese IX War Area continues demolition/rearguard fighting while shifting artillery, signals and service elements south of Changsha.

Liuyang defensive system is turned and collapses in stages; Japanese control is established by 15 May working center. Main Chinese formations disengage rather than accept encirclement. Liling/Chuzhou-axis pressure grows, reducing viable reinforcement routes into Changsha.

Ningxiang is taken/neutralized by 17 May working center; Xiangtan also falls or becomes operationally unusable to the Chinese on 17 May after planned evacuation/demolition. Changsha becomes operationally isolated, but the IX War Area heavy-command core is already southward.

Japanese 58th-Division-centered assault and flanking pressure enters Changsha after short concentrated preparation. Chinese local garrison conducts demolition and limited urban denial, then withdraws across/away from the Xiang where routes remain open. Changsha passes to Japanese operational control late 18 May working center; Yuelu/river crossings are not left intact.

position_state_18May.Xiangtan: JAPANESE_OPERATIONAL_CONTROL_OR_DENIED_TO_CHINA; rail/airfield facilities damaged and require repair

ground_losses_11_18May.interpretation: Japanese artillery/engineer/communications advantages and multi-axis geometry keep the exchange favorable, but Chinese pre-authorized force preservation prevents a large Changsha pocket. Urban loss is politically damaging without destroying IX War Area.

cumulative_ground_losses_28Apr_18May.guard: Arithmetic envelope across prior working adjudications and this window; not a national casualty census.

logistics_18May.engineer_state: Still coherent, but bridge/rail/airfield reconstruction now competes with continued southward movement. Xiang crossings and Changsha-Xiangtan facilities are damaged by demolition.
logistics_18May.captured_stock_credit: LOW. Chinese forces evacuate/destroy high-value ammunition, fuel, communications and aircraft-support stores; do not refill Japanese campaign stocks with fantasy capture tonnage.

phase_B_release_gate_18May.decision: HOLD_72_TO_120_HOURS_MINIMUM; no automatic Hengyang drive on city-capture day.
required: restore usable Xiang River crossing/ferry capacity
open Changsha-Xiangtan road/rail segments enough for sustained feed
advance fighter/recon servicing to captured airfield system without assuming instant heavy-bomber use
keep serviceable vehicle floor above roughly 4.3-5.0k working band
verify 14AF interdiction has not created multi-day ammunition/POL starvation
reassess Chinese force density Hengyang-Leiyang rather than extrapolating Changsha withdrawal
phase_B_release_gate_18May.meaning: Changsha capture completes Phase A. It does not itself authorize Phase B.
